title: Vertical-Positioning Microlearning
summary: A short-form sales-learning case study built as one Rise module with separate seaport and airport components, scenario practice, selective multimedia, and follow-up resources.

content.business_need: Help sellers build usable context for two industry settings without creating separate trainings or a broad vertical course.
content.audience: Internal sellers and channel partners who need concise industry context before discovery and positioning conversations.
learning_objectives: Recognize the operating context and common priorities within the seaport and airport settings.
Connect customer needs to relevant solution use cases at a sales-ready level.
Practice making a customer-facing decision in a short scenario.
Locate supporting resources for deeper follow-up instead of overloading the module.
content.role: Instructional designer and developer responsible for content scoping, learning structure, build, scenario design, multimedia integration, and review coordination.
content.design_approach: Organized one Rise module into distinct seaport and airport components. Both sections use a consistent pattern of context, use cases, practice, and resources while keeping the industry examples specific. Multimedia supports orientation without replacing the interactive learning.
content.development_process: Built one Rise microlearning module with two industry components, customer-facing scenario practice, and a short Colossyan presenter segment where narration added value. Coordinated internal QA and specialist review and revised wording, examples, scope, and media based on feedback.
outcomes: Delivered one focused Rise module with distinct seaport and airport components.
Used a consistent short-form pattern that connects context, use cases, practice, and follow-up resources.
Used specialist review and selective multimedia to keep the content useful without adding unnecessary depth.

source_material_notes: Generalized from documented industry-focused sales enablement work. Industry-specific proprietary messaging, internal screenshots, customer details, reviewer comments, dates, links, and source material are intentionally omitted.
